title: Effets d'une application prolongée de la loi spéciale en 2027
date_evidence: Publiée le 20 août 2026 | Mise à jour le 16 septembre 2026
key_claim: The IGF report finds that because of the 2027 electoral calendar a services-votés scenario of nine to twelve months cannot be excluded; the Treasury estimates the public balance could worsen by at least 0.5 point of GDP against 2026; investment grants to local authorities would not be paid; the special law has been used three times and never for more than six weeks; a full 2027 budget would be highly preferable.
frame_summary: The IGF argues that a prolonged special law is a costly and risky fall-back with no recovery of public finances, and that a real 2027 budget is far preferable, without taking a position on the route to adopt it.

title: Projet de loi de finances pour 2027 (n° 3210)
date_evidence: Enregistré à la présidence de l’Assemblée nationale le 1er octobre 2026

frame_summary: The government presents the 2027 bill as a consolidation budget that lowers the deficit from a revised 5.4% to 5.0% of GDP despite a heavier debt charge and a Middle East shock.

title: Le gouvernement et les ordonnances budgétaires : je t'aime, moi non plus !
date_evidence: Publié le 21 octobre 2026 à 13:20 | Modifié le 22 octobre 2026 à 11:11
key_claim: A constitutional-law analysis by Alexandre Guigue (Université Savoie Mont Blanc): under Article 47 the government may enact the budget by ordinance if Parliament has not ruled within 70 days, which falls on 17 December in 2026; the option was considered and dropped in January 2026; the author argues an ordinance is likely to bring censure but is more favourable to public finances than a special law.
frame_summary: The author argues the budget ordinance is a legally sound but politically costly route that is likely to return if the budget debate stalls, and that it may serve public finances better than a special law.

title: Budget initial, loi spéciale, ordonnances, 49.3, dissolution, affaires courantes : quelle sera la sauce budgétaire 2027 ?
key_claim: iFRAP argues the interaction of the budget tools (adoption, 49.3, rejection, ordinances, special law) will matter more than the budget's content; a definitive rejection of a text closes the ordinance route; the special law has been used three times (1979, 2025, 2026).
frame_summary: iFRAP, a liberal think tank, argues that the constitutional mechanics of adopting the 2027 budget, rather than its content, will drive French politics, and that rejection can shut off the ordinance route.
verbatim_quote: Jamais depuis 1958 les règles constitutionnelles d'adoption du budget n'auront autant pesé sur la vie politique.

title: Budget de la Sécu : l'Assemblée nationale rejette la partie « recettes », l'ensemble du texte va être transmis au Sénat
date_evidence: par Maxence Kagni Ludovic FAU, le Vendredi 23 octobre 2026 à 12:59, mis à jour le Vendredi 23 octobre 2026 à 15:40
key_claim: On 23 October 2026 the Assembly rejected the revenue part of the 2027 social security bill by 115 votes against to 1 for, so the whole original text goes to the Senate from 9 November; the social security deficit would reach 24 billion euros in the rejected version against a 12.7 billion euro target; the Prime Minister could use Article 49.3 or ordinances, which LCP calls a first for a budget.
frame_summary: LCP reports that the absence of any Assembly majority forces the social security bill to the Senate in its original form and leaves 49.3 or ordinances as the government's routes.

title: Date du vote du budget 2027 : le 3 novembre, deux semaines plus tard
key_claim: The Assembly's solemn vote on the revenue part of the 2027 finance bill is set for 3 November 2026 and the vote on the whole budget for 17 November; the 70-day period under Article 47 ends on 17 December, after which the government can enact the budget by ordinance; the ordinary session closes on 28 February 2027, four months earlier than usual, ahead of the presidential election.
frame_summary: NosParlementaires sets out the Assembly timetable as a sequence of hard constitutional dates that ends with an early close of the session for the presidential election.
verbatim_quote: la session s'arrête le 28 février 2027, quatre mois plus tôt que d'habitude, pour la présidentielle.
verbatim_list: aura lieu le mardi 3 novembre, deux semaines plus tard que prévu.

title: Dette : Moody's épargne la France, un léger répit, pas un vote de confiance
key_claim: Moody's kept France at Aa3 with a negative outlook on 23 October 2026, on the assumption that a 2027 budget reducing the deficit will be adopted; the French 10-year yield crossed 5.1% on 21 October against 3.2% before the war, with German Bunds near 3.4%; the Economy Minister calls adopting a responsible budget by year-end, bringing the deficit to 5%, intangible.
frame_summary: Euronews frames the Moody's decision as a reprieve conditional on the budget passing, with bond markets already pricing a France-specific confidence problem.
